1 September 2025 NEWNEWS FRS FROM THE BOOM THE BOARD ARD A monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners Welcome to the monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners. We are happy to share information on significant news and events in Ada County. Ryan Davidson - Commissioner Rod Beck - Chairman Tom Dayley - Commissioner REMEMBERED WITH COMPASSION Ada County honors those who died in our community and remain unclaimed Empathy and compassion help communities preserve their humanity. Both were on full display September 24, 2025 at the Terrace Lawn Memorial Gardens in Boise. The annual Remembered with Compassion event is a special memorial ceremony for those who died in Ada County without next of kin to plan for their burial or cremation. Part of this poignant ceremony included the reading of all the names of the 54 people, including children, who died without friends of family to honor their lives with funeral services. “We do this out of respect for those folks to give them some level of dignity.” Ada County Coroner Rich Riffle. During the FY24 Budget process, Ada County Commissioners approved $21,000 to be spent on the Columbarium – the above-ground structure designed for the reverential storage of funerary urns containing cremated remains. Thank you to the Ada County Coroner’s Office, Ada County Treasurer’s Office, and Cloverdale Funeral Home for organizing this beautiful event. Columbariums like the one picture above provide a permanent, maintained resting place and a serene location for families and friends to visit and honor loved ones who have been cremated.

3 SEPTEMBER IS NATIONAL RECOVERY MONTH Celebrating everyone who makes the journey of recovery possible Making a significant life change can be one of the most daunting challenges anyone faces. Now imagine that change includes freeing yourself from the chains of addiction. Here’s a somber statistic: Approximately 13% of the population in Ada County is affected either directly or indirectly by mental health and substance abuse disorders. It may not be you, but it could be someone you love. Boise’s 10th Annual Recovery Rally took place at Julia Davis Park on Saturday September 20, 2025. Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck read a proclamation designating the month of September 2025 as National Recovery Month. It’s a time set aside to celebrate everyone who makes the journey of recovery possible. The motto for Recovery Month is “Recovery is for everyone; Every person, every family, every community.” Thank you to our friends at Peer Wellness Center for helping to organize this annual event. Peer Wellness Center is a recovery community center that supports individuals wanting to initiate or maintain recovery from behavioral health and/or substance abuse issues. The non-profit organization has a variety of programs available to help individuals needing assistance including a food pantry, clothing closet, computer lab and recovery coaching services. Learn more about this recovery program at PEER WELLNESS CENTER Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck reads Proclamation designating September as National Recovery Month

4 “WE SEE YOU. WE BELIEVE YOU. WE ARE HERE FOR YOU.” Event recognizes Domestic Violence Awareness Month October is Domestic Violence Awareness Month. Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck joined Ada County Prosecutor Jan Bennetts, local Mayors, law enforcement officers, first responders, and our friends at the Women’s and Children’s Alliance on September 19, 2025 to acknowledge efforts being made locally to educate and protect victims. The event included the signing of a Proclamation recognizing the collaborative efforts made throughout the community to protect individuals and families. Each year in the United States, approximately one in three women and one in four men experience physical abuse from an intimate partner. Pictured L-R: Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck, WCA Executive Director Bea Black, Kuna Mayor Joe Stear, and Ada County Prosecutor Jan Bennetts

5 2025 MOSQUITO SEASON IN REVIEW Ada County Mosquito Abatement District (ACMAD) Surveillance and Adulticide operations wrapped up for the 2025 season on September 19th, marking an unofficial end to the season. Though there may still be a few mosquitoes flying around for a short while, cold nighttime temperatures as fall sets in will eliminate any risk of contracting West Nile virus (WNV) in Ada County for the rest of 2025. ACMAD detected the first WNV-positive mosquitoes of the season on July 24—a relatively late start. In total, 37 mosquito samples trapped throughout Ada County tested positive for WNV in 2025 (pending potential confirmations from inconclusive samples sent to the Idaho Bureau of Laboratories), compared to 27 last year. While that marks a 37% increase, the total falls within the typical range ACMAD sees year to year. The last detection occurred on September 10. To see where in Ada County WNV was detected in 2025, visit the Ada County Mosquito Tracker. Beyond WNV, ACMAD launched a new effort this summer to monitor for Aedes aegypti, an invasive mosquito capable of spreading diseases like dengue, Zika, and yellow fever. The species has recently been found in neighboring states, and on August 11, Canyon County trapped the first- ever Aedes aegypti in Idaho (later confirmed via DNA analysis). Aedes aegypti is often transported inadvertently through human activity—most commonly via potted plants or tires—making nurseries and tire shops a likely point of introduction. ACMAD has deployed specialized traps in these locations to help detect these mosquitoes as early as possible. While none have yet been found in Ada County, ACMAD plans to expand monitoring and prevention efforts to ensure the invasive species doesn’t gain a foothold locally. Samuel Brockway Ada County Weed Pest Mosquito Program and Education Specialist

6 NATIONAL PROCUREMENT INSTITUTE “Achievement of Excellence in Procurement” Award For the 5th consecutive year, Ada County Procurement has been awarded the prestigious Annual Achievement of Excellence in Procurement® (AEP) from the National Procurement Institute, Inc. (NPI). Ada County Procurement is the only Idaho procurement program to ever receive this award! The AEP Award is earned by agencies that demonstrate a commitment to procurement excellence. This annual program recognizes procurement organizations that embrace Innovation, Professionalism, Productivity, Leadership, and e-Procurement. The AEP program encourages the development of excellence as well as continued organizational improvement to earn the award annually. For 2025, there were 216 successful applicants including 85 cities, 48 counties, 23 special districts, 26 school districts, 15 higher education agencies, 7 state or provincial agencies and 12 others. Pictured L-R: Evan Amidan, Procurement Officer II Ryan Blaine, Procurement Officer I Tom Dayley, Ada County Commissioner Bob Perkins, Procurement Director Alyssa Ellington, Procurement Manager Kathy Corless, Procurement Analyst Robyn Swaney, Procurement Officer II Ken Sinclair, Fleet Manager Rod Beck, Ada County Commission Chairman Ryan Davidson, Ada County Commissioner

7 THE PARK AT EXPO IDAHO PROGRESS By the time you have the newsletter in hand – this area will look much different. That’s because work on The Park at Expo Idaho is happening fast. The Park at Expo Idaho is scheduled to open in the summer of 2026. This regional destination park will feature approximately 45 acres of nature trails, restored wetlands, a professional world-class skate park, a food truck area, nature playgrounds, and acres of outdoor space to connect with nature. Located right alongside the magnificent Boise River, The Park at Expo Idaho will incorporate sections of the Boise River Greenbelt - making everyone’s bicycle ride, walk, run or daily bike commute even more enjoyable. Make sure you follow us on Facebook for monthly construction updates featuring some impressive drone footage of this massive construction project. www.facebook.com/AdaCountyIdaho ADA COUNTY GOVERNMENT In addition to elected offices, Ada County government includes twelve individual departments. Each department provides important services to our residents in Star, Eagle, Meridian, Boise, Garden City, Kuna, and Unincorporated Ada County. These services include law enforcement protection, emergency preparedness, election services, parks & waterways, indigent services, juvenile services, solid waste management, the Western Idaho Fair, Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement and more. Learn more about the services provided to you by Ada County - www.adacounty.id.gov/

8 TOBIN BOLTER MEMORIAL KIDS’ DUATHLON DRAWS RECORD NUMBER OF PARTICIPANTS Little athletes everywhere! Energetic children of various ages participated in this year’s Tobin Bolter Memorial Kids’ Duathlon. The annual event, organized for the last nine years by Ada County Development Services, celebrates community, health, and the beautiful trails and open spaces that make Ada County such a vibrant community. In 2024, the event was renamed to honor fallen Ada County Sheriff’s Deputy Tobin Bolter, who was tragically killed in the line of duty on April 21, 2024. Deputy Bolter was just 27 years old. Deputy Bolter lived every day with purpose, treating others with respect and kindness. His memory remains an inspiration to those who knew and loved him. In recognition of his lifelong passion for running and athletics, the kids’ duathlon was renamed, ensuring his legacy continues to inspire young athletes.

9 CONGRATULATIONS ON 20 YEARS OF SERVICE Field Captain Jeremiah Wickham was recognized by the Ada County Commissioners for his 20 years of dedicated service to the citizens of Ada County on September 23, 2025. Jeremiah is a Boise High School grad who wanted to give back to his community and 20 years later, here he is. Congrats Jeremiah! Pictured L-R: Deputy Chief Jeremy Schabot, Ada County Chief Paramedic Shawn Rayne, Deputy Chief of Operations John Blake, Field Captain Jeremiah Wickham, Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck, Ada County Commissioner Tom Dayley We see a lot of uniforms at the Ada County Courthouse, including those of law enforcement, security guards, Marshals, and deputies. We also see a lot of people coming to court wearing a variety of .... outfits. What we don’t see often are tiaras and satin evening gowns. Jacque Cole was recognized with a 20-year Service Award with Ada County Paramedics this week. Why the gown and tiara? Jacque tells us it was part of an informal bet she had – if she reached twenty years, she’d wear a gown and tiara when she received her service award. Thank you, Jacque, for adding something lovely and fresh to the courthouse, and congratulations on your twenty years of exemplary service. Pictured L-R: Ada County Commissioner Tom Dayley, Billing Mgr. Linda Rosenwinkel, Deputy Chief of Operation John Blake, Captain Steve Cole, Jacque Cole, Chairman Rod Beck and Commissioner Ryan Davidson

10 DOGS MAKE EVERYTHING BETTER Go Team Idaho Therapy Dogs Visit the Ada County Courthouse Ada County Commissioner Tom Dayley was pleased to spend quality time with Go Team Therapy Dog Balin Hale last month. Balin and his four-legged buds are part of the Go Team Idaho Therapy Dogs program. The group is a non-profit organization that services our community by going to various places as requested to offer comfort, stress relief and joy. We’re not sure why - but the visits to the Ada County Courthouse always have a robust turnout. The dogs are deployed to foster a sense of calm and happiness. They make a world of difference. You can learn more about the program here: www.goteamdogs.org ADA COUNTY COURTHOUSE LOBBY CONSTRUCTION PROJECT UNDERWAY Twenty-three years ago, in 2002, when the new Ada County Courthouse on Front Street in Boise first opened, the county’s population was 322,000. Today our population is more than 572,000. Our courthouse is now serving more people than ever. During the FY25 budget cycle, the Ada County Commissioners approved the remodeling of the courthouse lobby. Site setup began on September 29, 2025, and the project should be done at the end of November 2025. The work area is enclosed with a temporary wall during the construction project. While this won’t affect your ability to enter or exit the courthouse there will be more noise than usual. Thank you for your understanding and cooperation as we work to enhance the courthouse’s lobby.
